subject: Latency spike + p95/p99 regressions on Hosted API — QuickShop production
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@quickshop.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: support+quickshop@quickshop.com
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: p95/p99 latency spike and throughput collapse on Hosted API (prod)

Karthik —

We started getting alerts around 08:40 PDT: p95 and p99 for our inference calls to redwood-hosted jumped ~2.5x and our token-per-second throughput dropped ~60% across a subset of model routes. Error rates for long-context requests also increased (502s). This began right after we saw a spike in 99th percentile latency for /v1/generate.

Impacted routes: model:open-xl:generate, model:open-xl:chat_v2.
Sample request_ids: 0a4b3c, 0a4b4d, 0a4b9f (attached file).

Quick timeline:
- 08:39:43 PDT: first alert (p99 > 3s)
- 08:45 — mass client-side retries
- 08:57 — visible TPS drop on our side, throughputs down to ~40% of baseline

Can you advise whether this is a QuickShop-side config change (we didn't change anything) or an issue on Redwood's hosted runtime? We need a mitigation path — SLA credit, rollback, or a fallback.

Thanks — this is high priority for our payments checkout feature.

Alex Morgan
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
QuickShop

- This started ~08:40 PDT.

Please keep me updated; this is now a customer escalation. If you need me to loop execs, let me know.

— Karthik

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Immediate: p95/p99 latency spike and throughput collapse on Hosted API (prod)

Karthik —

I'm looking at the serving telemetry. Short summary so far:
- There was a staged rollout this morning at 07:55 PDT of quantization-profile v2 for open-xl on the hosted pool in us-west. It included a kernel selection hint that prefers the new INT4 kernels on newer GPUs.
- Canary metrics initially looked fine, but we started to see divergence at ~08:30 on real traffic.

Evidence:
- Increased KV-cache churn and higher device memory pressure on a subset of pods (logs attached to internal ticket).
- p95 jumped ~2x and token-per-second (measured as tokens/s exported) dropped ~55% for long-context requests (>= 2k tokens). Short requests (<512 tokens) show minor impact.

Next steps I'm running now:
- Rollback quantization-profile v2 on the affected pool to v1 (target: within 30m).
- If rollback doesn't immediately restore TPS, we'll force-route QuickShop to an alt variant pinned to v1.

Rishi — can you confirm whether the new kernel selection path could be evicting high-KV-cache sessions or causing inefficient attention kernels for long sequences?

Laura
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 10:24:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Immediate: p95/p99 latency spike and throughput collapse on Hosted API (prod)

Laura/Karthik — quick technical notes from the runtime side. I'm attaching a diff of the kernel selection changes and a quick plot.

Summary of findings (initial):
- The INT4 kernel path introduces a slightly different KV layout that increases per-session memory when sequences exceed ~1.8k tokens. For smaller sequences it's fine, but for our long-context workloads (like QuickShop's checkout traces) it causes additional device memory copies and more frequent eviction/backfill cycles.
- Observed behavior: token-per-second metric drops because of increased per-step latency (attention kernel loop now has an extra memcpy on ~30% of steps). That explains the p99 spikes and TPS drop.
- Rollback plan: revert kernel-hint for open-xl on us-west pool -> re-enable legacy kernel for long-context paths. This should restore baseline throughput.

I've kicked the rollback (rolling restart of affected pods) at 10:29 PDT. ETA for measurable impact: 10–20 minutes, depending on request routing.

Attachments: kernel-change-diff.patch, tps_deltas_20270328.png

Alex — quick update: engineering identified a quantization + kernel-selection change rolled this morning that likely caused increased memory churn for long-context workloads. Rishi has initiated a rollback to the previous kernel path (legacy long-seq kernels) and we expect to see TPS and p99 improve within ~20 minutes.

What we'll do for QuickShop:
- Route your traffic to a stable variant pinned to the previous quant profile until we've validated the new path thoroughly.
- Post-mortem with root cause and mitigation plan by EOD Monday.
- We'll evaluate SLA compensation once we have the finished impact window.

I'll monitor and keep you posted once metrics look stable. Apologies for the disruption — we know this is sensitive for checkout flows.

— Karthik

Subject: QuickShop incident summary and next steps (post-mitigation)

Team / Alex —

Final summary after monitoring:
- Incident window: 2027-03-28T08:39:43-07:00 through 2027-03-28T11:03:12-07:00 (observed on QuickShop routes).
- Root cause: quantization-profile v2 rollout with kernel-selection hint that triggered additional memcpy/eviction behavior for long-context sequences on the us-west hosted pool.
- Impact: p95 increased up to 2.4x, p99 up to 2.8x; tokens-per-second dropped up to 60% for long-context requests; transient 502s observed when pod memory pressure was highest.
- Mitigation: rollback completed and QuickShop traffic pinned to legacy quant-profile. Observed TPS restored to within 5% of baseline within 25 minutes post-rollback.

Action items:
- Engineering to deliver a post-mortem (root cause, why canary missed signal, improved metrics + gating for kernel hints) by EOD Monday. (Owner: Laura, Rishi)
- CS to propose SLA credit calculation and formal apology (Owner: Marissa).
- Product to add a rollout safety check for long-context KV/cache-sensitive models (Owner: Product).

Alex — we appreciate the quick reports and the sample request ids; that helped us narrow things down. Marissa will follow up about credit and PM will invite your team to the post-mortem review if you'd like to attend.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
